# phase-119 — Expose the last value as `$_` and name sessions

## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
Redblue binds the result of each line to `_` (src/repl/mod.rs inserts it under the name `_` after printing `= <value>`), but there is no way to ask what it holds, refer to it as a value, or capture it. Ipp exposes `.last` and `$_` (REPL_AUDIT.md 2.16) for the same need. `:session` is also missing — Ipp has it at 2.23 — so a session cannot be named, saved under a name, or restored, which makes a debugging session that took twenty minutes unrepeatable. `:restore` exists in Redblue but with nothing to name.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Make the last value usable, not merely printed: `$_` resolves to it inside a program, and `:last` prints it explicitly. Add `:session <name>` to label the current session and `:sessions` to list the labels used this week. Keep `_` working exactly as it does — this is additive, and any change to the existing binding is a behaviour change this phase must not make.

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `$_` in a following program evaluates to the previous line's value, asserted against a literal expected number
- [ ] `$_` after an error line is the last SUCCESSFUL value, not the error, and the test pins which
- [ ] `:last` prints the same value `$_` resolves to, so the two cannot disagree
- [ ] `:last` on a session where nothing has succeeded yet raises a catchable error naming the condition rather than printing nothing
- [ ] `:session <name>` labels the session and `:sessions` lists every label used, in deterministic order
- [ ] labelling a session does not change any program's behaviour - asserted by running an identical program before and after
- [ ] the existing `_` binding still works exactly as before, asserted by a test that predates this phase and passes unmodified
- [ ] edge_* cases cover a first-line `$_`, a `$_` used before any successful line, a session name with spaces, and a label containing characters a command word may not carry
